title: Excessive decommission signal caused tier starvation and fanout amplification (postmortem)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2026-02-09 at ~22:18 UTC an automated decommission job erroneously marked a subset of nodes in a single region as decommissioned. The control plane interpreted the signal as an immediate drain and propagated a wide routing update that caused tier-level capacity starvation. Traffic shifted to fallback model variants and lower-tier pools, creating a fanout amplification where requests were retried and re-routed across tiers, producing elevated tail latency and increased error rates for hosted API customers. Impact lasted for ~40 minutes with partial recovery after manual mitigation and automated throttling adjustments.

Why this matters: The incident exposed a sequence of interacting control-plane and routing-policy assumptions (decommission==drain immediate, no soft grace window, aggressive RTT-based tier demotion) that together turn a local maintenance event into a global availability perturbation. We need to treat decommission signals as higher-cost control events with safety guardrails to avoid cascading fallbacks and customer-visible degradations.
timeline: 2026-02-09 22:18 UTC - Automated decommission job (scale-manager) applied decommission tag to ~26 nodes in eu-west-3 due to a mis-scoped Cassandra query used by a maintenance script.
2026-02-09 22:19 UTC - Region control-plane published a drain intent; routing-service picked up state and issued immediate tier demotion policy for the affected shards.

2026-02-09 22:19-22:25 UTC - Traffic shifted from dedicated and high-tier pools to lower-tier general pools and fallback model variants. Some requests were retried by client-side SDKs and by the service when encountering transient capacity errors, causing amplification.
2026-02-09 22:25 UTC - Monitoring alerted: SLO error budget burn and spike in P95/P99 latency for generation endpoints; first incident page triggered.
2026-02-09 22:30 UTC - Oncall began traffic steering to isolate eu-west-3 and temporarily disable immediate demotion rules; manual un-decommission started for 10 nodes judged healthy.
2026-02-09 22:42 UTC - A temporary routing throttle was applied to prevent broad fallback fanout; feature flag toggled to add 30s hysteresis to decommission->drain path.
2026-02-09 23:00 UTC - Majority of traffic stabilized; residual errors cleared by 23:10 UTC. Post-incident cleanup completed on 2026-02-10.
root_cause:
A maintenance script in scale-manager constructed a Cassandra query without a region scoping predicate; it returned nodes scheduled for future decommission in the same partition and those nodes were incorrectly treated as immediate decommission targets. The downstream control-plane treated the decommission tag as a synchronous drain signal (no soft-grace/hysteresis), and our routing policy aggressively demotes tiers on perceived capacity loss, with no amplification controls for simultaneous multi-tier fallback.

Contributing factors: (1) Lack of scoped queries in scale-manager maintenance job; (2) Decommission tag semantics conflated planned and immediate drains; (3) Routing policy lacked a soft window/hysteresis and did not rate-limit fallback fanout; (4) Monitoring thresholds were tuned for steady-state, not fast churn, delaying automated mitigation triggers; (5) SDK client retry behavior compounded amplification during tier swapping.
impact: Approx 40 minutes of elevated P95/P99 latency and transient 10-20% error rates for generation endpoints in eu-west and traffic-crossing customers. Estimated customer-visible requests affected: ~0.3% of hosted API calls during the window; several enterprise customers reported degraded response times and filed support tickets. No data loss, no security breach.
mitigation_and_remediation: Immediate - Rolled back decommission marks for healthy nodes and isolated eu-west-3 from automated maintenance pipeline.
Immediate - Applied routing throttle and enabled a conservative hysteresis flag on decommission->drain transition (30s) to prevent instant tier demotion.
Short-term - Temporarily relaxed client-side retry policy via SDK hotfix to avoid amplification during retries (v2.1.3 rolled out to hosted SDKs).
Short-term - Tuned monitoring alert thresholds to detect sudden tier demotion and fanout amplification earlier.
Long-term - Patch scale-manager to enforce region-scoped queries and add unit/integration tests to prevent regression.
Long-term - Update routing-policy to add rate-limiting on fallback propagation, multi-tier fanout caps, and configurable grace windows for planned vs immediate decommissions.
Long-term - Introduce a decommission tombstone TTL and a state classification: planned | draining | draining-protected with explicit operator confirmation for wide-scale drains.
Long-term - Add chaos tests and a simulated maintenance waveform to our staging environment to validate routing hysteresis and fallback caps under realistic churn.

decision_log: 2026-02-10 - Decided to treat decommission tags as soft by default; immediate drains now require explicit 'force' attribute or operator confirmation.
2026-02-17 - Adopted fallback cap design: maximum 2-tier demotions within 60 seconds for any given shard without explicit operator override.
2026-02-22 - Chose to roll SDK retry backoff hotfix as immediate customer-facing mitigation prior to full routing policy change.
2026-02-28 - Approved scale-manager query hardening and additional integration tests; merge scheduled for runtime-1.22 release.
notes_and_tradeoffs: We deliberately chose a 30s hysteresis to balance responsiveness for genuine failures vs safety for planned maintenance. Shorter windows risk still triggering amplification; longer windows delay failover for true outages.
Fanout caps reduce immediate capacity elasticity; to compensate we will expose a controlled override for high-priority customers and for verified incident scenarios.
SDK retry reduction improves platform behavior during churn but may surface transient errors to client apps sooner; we'll coordinate with SDK consumers for broader rollout and guidance.
Adding tombstone TTL complicates operational visibility for long-decommission cycles; we will include metadata and operator tooling to query historical tombstones.
These mitigations prioritize platform stability and SLO preservation over instantaneous failover aggressively favored previously.
